## 🔒 Claimed — `domain:ui` execution seat (objectui)

- **Session:** `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM` · **Branch:** `claude/issue-7126-edit-widgets-error-prop`
- **Build tier:** opus (⚠️ Fable 5 quota exhausted; the exemption lowers the *build* tier only)

### ✅ Held out of rotation on purpose until now — the blocker landed 20 minutes ago

This card was filed by #7008's implementer and **deliberately not dispatched** when it appeared, because its end-to-end pin needs `FieldEditWidget` to actually **deliver** `error` — and it did not. **PR #7128 landed as `f08bcd9af`** (`git log origin/main`), verified: `packages/fields/src/widgets/toHostProps.ts` is on `main`, with `toDomProps.ts` as the pre-dating control.

⇒ The delivery now exists, so a test asserting *"an inline `text` control that failed validation reports `aria-invalid`"* can be written against a real path instead of a hypothetical one. **Dispatching now is the point at which the card became answerable, not merely available.**

**Not clause ②** — widgets reading a prop already declared on `FieldWidgetComponentProps` and already delivered. Nothing enters or leaves a published surface.

### The measurement, and the one trap inside it

Of the **27** distinct components in `EDIT_WIDGETS`, **21** read `error`. ⚠️ Six appeared not to — but **`UserField` is a FALSE zero**: it renders `LookupField` with a props spread, so it delivers `error` transitively and does mark. A naive census reports six and is wrong about one.

⇒ The real population is **five**: `TextField`, `BooleanField` (`boolean`, `toggle`), `DateField`, `DateTimeField`, `TimeField`. ⚠️ **Re-derive it anyway** — the census was taken before #7128 landed, and `git grep` against an explicit ref, never the shared checkout.

⭐ **`text` being in that set is what makes this p2 rather than tidiness**: the kanban `RequiredFieldsDialog` renders whatever types the column made required, so a required *text* field still reports no `aria-invalid` even after #7128. That is the same live a11y defect #7008 closed for the other 21, still open for these five.

### Fences

- ⛔ **This buys the a11y MARKING only.** The #3222 slot drives `aria-invalid`; it renders no text. Do not claim a visible message appears.
- ⚠️ Match the shape the 21 already use — read the existing readers (`NumberField` is the closest precedent, `aria-invalid={!!error || !!refusal}` from #7002) rather than inventing a new spelling. Five widgets converging on one existing idiom, ⛔ not five variations.
- ⚠️ Some of these are **composite** controls (`BooleanField` may be a switch, `DateField` a picker). Where there is no single focusable input, say what you marked and why — ⛔ do not mark a wrapper `div` and call it done. #7128's implementer hit exactly this reasoning on the kanban dialog's `label` workaround.
- ⛔ Do not touch `toDomProps` / `toHostProps` / `FieldEditWidget` — that is #7008's landed work and its three compile-time assertions now partition the contract.

## 🟢 Landed — `e8e4c4df5`

PR objectstack-ai/objectui#7141 merged at 05:32:13Z; `main` advanced to `e8e4c4df5f51fc3a1d5ffc678881d3480f97a70e`. `Fixes` closed this card.

*fix(fields): the last five inline widgets read the delivered `error` slot*

### Landing verified by content, with two controls

Never by sha — a squash merge creates a new commit, and even `main` landing *on* a queue sha is not proof the diff arrived. Probed against `origin/main` in a local checkout rather than code search, because a search index lags a fresh push and would produce a **false zero** on exactly this kind of check.

| probe | expect | got |
|---|---|---|
| SUBJECT — `aria-invalid={!!error}` across the five widgets | 7 (2/2/1/1/1) | **7** ✅ |
| CONTROL 1 — `NumberField.tsx` word-boundary `error` | non-zero (was 5) | **5** ✅ |
| CONTROL 2 — same string, same file, at the pre-merge sha `0d4c7890d` | 0 | **0** ✅ |
| both new test files on `main` | present | **both** ✅ |

Control 2 is the one that carries the weight: it is a **differential** control — identical string, identical path, two revisions, 2 vs 0. Together with Control 1 proving the instrument returns non-zero when there is something to find, the zero at the old sha is a real zero rather than a broken query.

### Why this one earned the arm without a round trip

**The census was re-taken, not remembered.** The card's population was measured *before* PR objectui#7128 landed. It was re-derived here at `f08bcd9af`, after the blocker. That is the difference between a population and a memory of one — and this seat has already been burned by citing a merged PR's `head.sha`, which does not exist on `main` at all.

**Every apparent zero was opened rather than counted.** `UserField` scores 0 on a word-boundary `error` match, and that is a **FALSE ZERO**: its entire body delegates the whole props object onward, so it marks transitively and always did. I had verified that line directly before dispatch and the dev caught it independently. A census trusting its six zeroes would have "fixed" a widget that was never broken. Pinning it as a permanent CONTROL case in the new sweep is the durable answer — nobody can now quietly "repair" it.

**The ablation asserted the passing count, not just the red.** Predicted `19 failed | 2 passed (21)` before running; observed exactly that, with the two survivors being precisely the two control cases that do not depend on the five widgets. A suite collapsed to "no tests" produces red with no survivors and *looks stronger*. Mutation proven by marker count **and** blob hash; restore proven by state — `git diff HEAD`, `git diff --cached`, `git status --short` all empty — never by an editor's exit code.

**A NOT MEASURED was reported as such.** `type-check` first returned a wall of `TS2307: Cannot find module '@object-ui/components'` across untouched files. That is an unbuilt dependency closure — the *absence* of a reading, not a red. It was named as NOT MEASURED, the closure was built, and the verdict came from the re-run.

### The PM boundary I set was falsified — correctly, and without widening the PR

I fenced the population at `EDIT_WIDGETS`. Structurally wrong: `InlineFieldInput` renders four widgets onto the same inline surface that are not in `EDIT_WIDGETS` at all. The dev measured them on the same instrument with the same live control, found `ImageField` / `AvatarField` / `FileField` already marking, and found `SignatureField`'s zero to be a **documented verdict** (no keyboard path on the canvas) matching its `NOT_APPLICABLE` registry row — then left the PR at five widgets and filed nothing.

Reporting a falsified fence that turns out to have no gap behind it, instead of hiding it *or* expanding scope on it, is the outcome I want. Same judgement on objectui#7128's now-false doc comment: corrected in place with a pointer to where the `text` case lives, not deleted, because that sentence is the reason `select` was originally chosen.

### ⚠️ One sub-claim stands as UNCONFIRMED, not verified

`check:sdui-registration-pins` returned `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 2) locally — correctly classified NOT MEASURED rather than green. The report then stated "CI builds the console and runs it." **I could not find a check run under that name among the 30**, so it may be a step inside `Build & E2E` or may not run on PRs at all. I did not confirm it either way.

I armed regardless because that claim is not load-bearing: this diff **registers nothing**, so a registration-pin gate has no subject in it whether or not CI executes it. Recording it explicitly so the unconfirmed half is never later remembered as checked.

### Ledger

- Clause ② **not engaged** — consumes the slot objectui#7008 / PR objectui#7128 landed; no new export, no parse accept/reject change.
- `toDomProps.ts`, `toHostProps.ts`, `FieldEditWidget.tsx` untouched — objectui#7008's three compile-time assertions still partition the contract.
- Marking only. The visible message stays with the host; nothing invisible became visible.
- This also closes out the objectui#6868 overclaim: that landing note said the `error` threading "buys the a11y marking" when I had verified producer and consumer but **not the factory seam between them**. Fourteen direct renders did deliver; the `FieldEditWidget` path did not. objectui#7128 fixed the seam, and this card fixed the five widgets that still ignored it.
